## Description

The classic slipper-shaped ciliate (~180 × 50 µm here, up to ~300 µm) that eats bacteria through its
oral groove. It backs off when it bumps into something (avoiding reaction), gathers where there is
CO₂ and discharges trichocysts when attacked. The posterior pole is more pointed than the anterior.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `moss` (weight 0.15), `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 20 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

The reference ciliate: helical swimming, [avoiding reaction](../../mechanics/behavioural-responses.md),
[acid trap](../../mechanics/behavioural-responses.md#avoiding-reaction-and-acid-trap) (Jennings), chemokinesis,
conjugation with mating types, and an oral groove as a body notch. It eats at its **measured**
ingestion rate, and its bacterial capture radius is calibrated so that the plate and the culture eat
the same. Validated: µmax on the plate and in the culture, Jennings, functional response, Gause
monoculture plateau.

## Literature

- Gause G.F. (1934) *The Struggle for Existence*. Williams & Wilkins, fig. 22 (own logistic fit to the
  gauseR data: r = 0.946 ± 0.109/day, K = 203; temperature not verified, 26 °C assumed).
- Applied Water Science (2013), doi:10.1007/s13201-013-0130-1 (~26·10³ bacteria per individual per
  hour; 106 nL/h at ~2.5·10⁸ bacteria/mL).
- Hansen P.J., Bjørnsen P.K., Hansen B.W. (1997) Zooplankton grazing and growth: scaling within the 2–2,000-µm body size range. Limnol. Oceanogr. 42: 687–704.
- Kiørboe T. (2011) How zooplankton feed: mechanisms, traits and trade-offs. Biol. Rev. 86: 311–339.
- Jennings H.S. (1906) *Behavior of the Lower Organisms*. Columbia Univ. Press.
- Kitching J.A. (1938) (contractile vacuole period, 5–10 s).
- Stock C. et al. (2002) J. Exp. Biol. 205: 1171 (cytosol osmolarity).

## Not implemented yet

- It does not win/lose against *P. aurelia* for the right reason ([bug](../../bugs/gause-aurelia-does-not-win.md)).
- No galvanotaxis or gravitaxis.
- No macronuclear amitosis or autogamy.
- Helix radius and period are estimates (of the order of Bullington 1925 and Jennings 1906).
- Trichocysts are a defence gene, not discharged organelles that can be counted.
- Contractile vacuole period in fresh water estimated; cytosol osmolarity taken from *P. caudatum*.

## Unique and shared mechanics

Defines the ciliate behaviour shared by most ciliates; the acid trap is shared with *P. aurelia* and
*P. tetraurelia*. See [validation](../../validation/README.md).
